messages.author: d7a934c791b29498
messages.subject: rhdfs can't use hdfs.init()
parts:
I set up Hadoop 1.2.1 in pseudo-distributed mode.

I used the standard settings for the core-site.xml, namely:
 <value>hdfs://localhost:9000</value>
I verified that ssh worked and ran the example jobs correctly with plain Hadoop.
I verified that R had everything necessary for rmr2 and rhdfs.

> library(rhdfs)
Loading required package: rJava

HADOOP_CMD=/home/user/hadoop-1.2.1/bin/hadoop

Be sure to run hdfs.init()
> hdfs.init()
13/10/23 15:22:12 INFO ipc.Client: Retrying connect to server: localhost/127.0.0.1:9000. Already tried 0 time(s); retry policy is RetryUpToMaximumCountWithFixedSleep(maxRetries=10, sleepTime=1 SECONDS)
...
13/10/23 15:22:21 INFO ipc.Client: Retrying connect to server: localhost/127.0.0.1:9000. Already tried 9 time(s); retry policy is RetryUpToMaximumCountWithFixedSleep(maxRetries=10, sleepTime=1 SECONDS)
Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl,  :
  java.net.ConnectException: Call to localhost/127.0.0.1:9000 failed on connection exception: java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused

I looked at some webpages from people who had gotten similar errors and tried some tactics that had worked for them.

Some people had success from modifyi        <property>
                <name>dfs.permissions</name>
                <value>false</value>
        </property>
ng their .xml files under conf.
For example, some added the property
        <property>
                <name>dfs.permissions</name>
                <value>false</value>
        </property>
to hdfs-site.xml.


 Others modified /etc/hosts to remove IPv6. 

I imitated the above measures but continued to have connection problems.

The Michael Noll tutorial at:

advises editing the /etc files to cause the IPv4 stack to get priority.

He also advises changing the port numbers in the conf .xml files.  Testing his suggestions will require a reboot.

messages.subject: Re: rhdfs can't use hdfs.init()
parts:
Fixed!

I had been following suggestions from old tutorials about pseudo-distributed mode.  These old tutorials did not use complicated versions of the .xml files.

However, when the .xml files are easy, for some reason, the namenode shuts down with the following errors in the logs:

. . .
The good news is that the .xml files can be fixed to prevent this namenode shutdown.

In particular, I modded hdfs-site.xml to include:

 <property>
  <name>dfs.name.dir</name>
  <value>/home/user/bigdataname</value>
 </property>
<property>
   <name>dfs.data.dir</name>
   <value>/home/user/hadoopdata</value>
</property>

and as a result, basic mapreduce works within R with to.dfs and from.dfs
